subject: Sample project prompt + reviewer scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@gmail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sample project prompt + reviewer scheduling

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for interviewing with the Infra team last week. As discussed, attached is the short sample project we use for backend/inference engineer candidates. High-level: a focused coding + writeup exercise (~2–4 hours).

Key details:
- Attachment: sample_project_prompt.pdf (see Drive link below if you prefer)
- Deadline: submit by EOD Wednesday, Mar 3 (48 hours from now). If you need a short extension, let us know promptly.
- Submission: send a single .zip with code + README to this thread; filename should be lastname_firstname_submission.zip
- Estimated reviewer time: ~45 minutes each; reviewers: Aditya (tech lead) and Lauren (hiring manager)
- Debrief: we plan a 30-minute internal readout to sync on grading and next steps — tentative window Thu Mar 4, 11:00–12:30 PT. Aditya will confirm availability.

Helpful links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/sample-project-prompt
Grading rubric attached (grading_template.xlsx) — we prioritize correctness, clarity of reasoning, and tradeoff discussion.

Please reply to confirm you received the prompt and whether the deadline works. If anything in the prompt is unclear, ask here and we’ll clarify.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Hiring Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample_project_prompt.pdf, grading_template.xlsx

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@gmail.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sample project prompt + reviewer scheduling

Thanks — I got the prompt and the rubric. I should be able to complete it by EOD Wednesday, but could I request a short one-day extension to Thursday EOD if needed? I have a prior commitment Wednesday afternoon that might cut into the time window.

Also: quick clarification on the expected language/runtime — Node or Python are both fine? I’ll plan Python unless you prefer otherwise.

Cheers,
Jordan Miles
(he/him)

Jordan — thanks for the quick reply. A one-day extension to Thu Mar 4 EOD is fine — please confirm if you’ll take that option. Python is perfect.

Aditya & Lauren — can you both pencil in a 30-minute internal debrief Friday Mar 5 at 10:00 PT if that works? That gives us a day to review submissions and coordinate feedback. If not, propose two alternate 30-minute slots. I’ll create a calendar invite once we lock a time.

Jordan — when you submit, please: (1) attach the zip to this thread, and (2) upload the repo to a private GitHub link if you’re comfortable (we’ll only use it for evaluation).

Thanks,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sample project prompt + reviewer scheduling

All good from my side — Friday Mar 5 10:00 PT works. I’ll block 30 minutes: 10:00–10:30 PT.

A couple of notes for grading to keep consistent:
- Prioritize correctness and tests; partial credit for well-reasoned tradeoffs.
- For the writeup, look for clarity on latency/throughput considerations for an inference runtime; short bullet section ok.
- I’ll use grading_template.xlsx and add comments there.

Marissa: once Jordan submits, I’ll take first pass and add scores/comments; Lauren can then add hire/no-hire recommendation and we’ll sync at the debrief.

Thanks,
Aditya

P.S. I added my Calendly link for any quick sync: https://calendly.com/aditya-rau/reviewer-debrief-30m
